description: Find out which fields your real payloads actually populate. Across a batch of documents it reports, per location, how often it is present, how often it holds anything, and every type it appears as. A location that is a string in some documents and a number in others is named, which no schema check on a single payload would reveal. Pay 90000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

items.description: Any JSON value you supply. Nothing is fetched, so this works on payloads nothing could reach.

expect_pointers.description: Pointers you expect to be present and populated everywhere. Each shortfall is reported as a finding.

treat_null_as_absent.description: Whether an explicit null counts as absent. Defaults to true, which is what most pipelines mean.

name: json_field_coverage_audit

always_present.description: Locations present in every document, which is what a schema could safely mark required.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of the input was not analysed, which is a different problem from input that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing below is bounded.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the exact location.

findings_by_code.description: Counts per code, for triage without reading the list.

never_populated.description: Locations that appear but never hold anything, which is usually a field nobody fills.

not_examined.description: Named reasons anything was left unexamined: a bound reached, an unsupported keyword, an unresolvable reference, or findings beyond the listing cap.

passed.description: True only when every expectation held, every location was consistently typed, and every document was fully examined.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

title: JSON Field Coverage Audit
